commit.message:
Add BLUETTI Modbus integration

Adds local Modbus TCP access to BLUETTI power stations (Balco260, EP2000),
alongside the existing cloud integration (PR #180440), following the same
pattern as the SolarEdge Modbus integration (#180508): borrows a shared
ModbusUnit from the modbus integration rather than owning its own
connection, using the bluetti-modbus library for device decoding.

Sensor platform only in this PR, to keep it reviewable - binary_sensor,
switch, select and diagnostics are each their own follow-up.

Tested against a real Balco260 (48/48 fields decoded correctly, including
enum and string fields).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Address review feedback: identity, enum states, scope, quality_scale

- Stop deriving unique_id from host/port/unit_id (an IP can change and
  isn't a stable device identity); use the documented "unique data"
  pattern (_async_abort_entries_match) instead, on both the user and
  reconfigure steps. Device/entity identifiers now key off entry_id.
- Decode enum-typed fields (inverter status/fault/warning) as proper
  ENUM sensors with translated state options, instead of leaking the
  library's own Enum repr as the entity state.
- Drop the on/off switches and configurable SoC limits from the sensor
  platform - they belong on switch/number once those platforms exist,
  not as sensors that would need removing later.
- Correct two quality_scale.yaml entries that were copied from the
  cloud integration without rechecking: the discovery exemption
  (devices here are not added via a cloud account) and
  entity-disabled-by-default (several diagnostic entities are
  plausible candidates, not yet triaged - marked todo).
- Fix the AddEntitiesCallback type on the sensor platform's
  async_setup_entry to AddConfigEntryEntitiesCallback.
- Remove icons.json (its only entries were for the now-removed switch
  fields).
- Add EP2000 setup coverage and a reconfigure-onto-another-entry's-
  endpoint test.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Identify devices by serial number where the device reports one

Balco260 now exposes a real serial number over Modbus (bluetti-modbus
0.1.3, following BLUETTI support confirming the register). Use it as
the config entry's unique_id instead of relying solely on host/port/
unit_id: catches the same device re-added at a new address, and
reconfiguring onto an address that answers as a different device is
now rejected outright rather than silently adopted.

Device types with no serial field yet (EP2000 today) fall back to the
existing host/port/unit_id link-matching, which now also always runs
in addition to the serial check - a link already claimed by a
different entry is rejected either way, serial or not.

Also drop a defensive None-check in sensor.py's async_setup_entry:
every name from device.field_names() is guaranteed to have a field via
device.get_field() (same dict, by construction), so replaced the
silent filter with an assert that documents the invariant instead of
masking a violation that can't actually happen.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Use bluetti-modbus's own retry-aware update instead of reimplementing it

bluetti-modbus 0.1.4 adds BluettiDevice.async_update_with_retry(),
moving the transient-busy retry this coordinator used to implement
itself into the library (bluetti-community/bluetti-modbus#33) -
integrations should be thin wrappers over the library, not reimplement
behavior the library already owns.

The coordinator just calls it now; no observable behavior change, and
none of the existing tests needed updating (they were already testing
outcomes, not the retry's internal call structure).

Co-Authored-By: Claude Sonnet 5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix CI: prettier key order in strings.json, stale bluetti-modbus pin

prettier requires strings.json's top-level keys (and each state map's
keys) sorted alphabetically; move selector after exceptions and sort
d_inverter_status.state accordingly. requirements_all.txt still pinned
bluetti-modbus==0.1.2 from before the manifest bump to 0.1.4, which is
why CI's mypy job resolved BluettiDevice without async_update_with_retry.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Address remaining review feedback: identity, read plan, EP2000 coverage

- Re-check the configured serial after every successful refresh, not only
  at setup, so an address/unit reassignment cannot silently publish a
  different physical device's data under the original entry.
- Narrow the device to its used fields via restrict_fields() at setup, so
  the excluded switch/limit fields are dropped from the actual Modbus read
  plan, not just from entity creation.
- Add an EP2000 sensor snapshot test, matching Balco260's coverage of
  model-specific entity generation.
- Note, rather than guess at, the real limit on model validation: EP2000's
  register map is a near-subset of Balco260's at identical addresses, so a
  successful probe cannot tell them apart without a distinguishing register
  confirmed against real EP2000 hardware.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Retry a transient busy probe; distinguish a link conflict from cannot_connect

_async_validate() called async_update() directly, so a transient
acknowledge/busy response failed the probe even though setup and polling
already retry it once via async_update_with_retry(). Separately,
async_get_temporary_unit() raising HomeAssistantError means the address is
already claimed by another entry with different link settings - a
deterministic conflict the user needs to fix, not a transient failure
"cannot_connect" tells them to retry.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Catch TimeoutError from the config-flow probe too

async_update_with_retry()'s own internal timeout budget expiring
raises a bare TimeoutError, not a ModbusError - _async_validate() only
caught ModbusError, so a probe that ran past that budget would crash
the config flow instead of surfacing cannot_connect.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Update the docs PR reference: #47711 was superseded by #47718

#47711 targeted the wrong base branch (current instead of next, since
this integration hasn't merged yet) and was closed in favor of #47718,
opened from the same branch against the right base.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Expose the serial number as device info, not a plain sensor

Balco260's serial doesn't change and isn't a measurement - it belongs
on the device's own info page (DeviceInfo.serial_number), matching
convention, not as a polled sensor entity. Uses entry.unique_id (the
serial confirmed at config-flow time) rather than a fresh register
read, since DeviceInfo is built before the coordinator's first refresh
runs.

d_serial stays in the read plan (unlike the switch/limit fields in
EXCLUDED_FIELDS): the coordinator's per-poll identity check still
needs it. Only entity creation skips it now, via a new,
sensor.py-local _ENTITY_EXCLUDED_FIELDS - restrict_fields() must not
touch it, or the identity check would never see a fresh value again.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Fix syntax error in the config-flow probe's exception handler

except ModbusError, TimeoutError: is Python 2 syntax and does not
parse - a typo from adding the TimeoutError catch without parenthesizing
the tuple.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Exclude fault/warning sensors until the library can decode real values

bluetti-modbus 0.1.4's InverterFault and InverterWarning enums each define
only their zero member, so a real, non-zero fault or warning code has
nothing to decode to. Excluded from both the read plan and entity creation
until the library represents the actual bitmaps, rather than shipping a
sensor that goes unknown exactly when it would matter.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

Key device identity and entity unique IDs off the confirmed serial

Balco260 entries already store their confirmed serial as entry.unique_id;
identifiers and unique IDs were still keyed on entry_id regardless,
making them integration-instance-specific rather than device-specific.
Prefer the serial where the model reports one, falling back to entry_id
only for a model with none (EP2000), matching the pattern already used by
solaredge_modbus.

Co-Authored-By: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>
